messages:
secret-scanner-bot: High confidence secret detected in repo `payments/service-tests` at commit abc123 — file `tests/fixtures/id_rsa` contains what looks like an RSA private key. :rotating_light:
sec-oncall: Marking P1. Creating incident TICK-458. Please stand by for containment steps.
sara: Ugh. Which environments use that repo? Is it pinned anywhere? :eyes:
ben: It's only used by the payments integration test job in CI. No prod deploys. That said, some infra service accounts are referenced in docs there — checking now.
maya: If it's a raw private key we need to rotate anything that used it and remove from history. First action: block CI artifact access and disable the test job to stop any circulation. @devops-bot can you pause the pipeline?
devops-bot: Pausing `payments-integration` pipeline... ✅ paused.
josh: Quick question: do we have evidence the key was used externally? Logs show no outgoing SSH to unknown hosts from test runners but I'll dig deeper.
sara: Good. Next, rotate any creds tied to that key and remove the file from the repo history. We should avoid naive `git rm` only. Need a history rewrite plan + PR + approvals.
ben: Suggested sequence: 1) identify which service/account (if any) corresponds to the key, 2) rotate credentials (or confirm none exist), 3) use `git filter-repo` to excise the file, push to a new branch, and coordinate a fast-forward force with dev leads. Also run full repo scan after rewrite.
sec-oncall: Agreed. josh, if logs show no usage, we still treat as compromised. Owner for rotation: @ben. Owner for repo rewrite: @maya. Owner for follow-up scans + retro: @sara.
maya: Repo rewrite commands for reference:
```
pip install git-filter-repo
git clone --mirror git@github.com:redwood/payments.git
cd payments.git
git filter-repo --invert-paths --path tests/fixtures/id_rsa
git push --force origin refs/heads/main
```
We should coordinate a one-hour freeze to avoid conflicts.
sara: Also add required pre-merge check to CI to fail if `tests/fixtures/` contains private key patterns. Add a suppressible policy for known safe test keys (but default off).
ben: For rotation, if it's an SSH key for a deploy user we should revoke the key in the authorized_keys store and generate a new keypair. If any KMS-wrapped secrets were created from this key material, rewrap with new CMK and rotate.
josh: I've checked runners and artifact storage. No evidence of external exfil. There was a single artifact retention copy in the CI cache from 3 days ago — I've deleted it and revoked that cache snapshot token.
sec-oncall: Update incident ticket TICK-458 with actions and ETA. Please paste the git rewrite PR link and list of rotated credentials once done.
maya: I'll open PR with the rewritten history and a short writeup. Notifying all repo collaborators to pull with `git fetch && git reset --hard origin/main` after we force-push.
sara: Post-incident controls: 1) tighten RBAC on who can push to repo (branch protection + 2 approvers), 2) enable pre-receive hook scanning for key patterns, 3) periodic repo leak scans scheduled daily for high-priv repos.
ben: I'll rotate any related service accounts and update our internal KMS rotation playbook to include a rewrap step when private keys are exposed.
josh: Running a full historical scan across org for similar fixtures now — will post results in TICK-458.
sec-oncall: Thanks everyone — please post status updates in the ticket. Once PR is merged and creds rotated, we'll remove P1 flag and move to postmortem.
sec-oncall: Next steps owner summary:
- ben: credential rotation (ETA 2h)
- maya: repo rewrite & force-push + PR (ETA 1h)
- josh: artifact/logs audit + org scan (ETA 3h)
- sara: follow-up controls + postmortem (ETA EOD)

sara: Also, add an action item to update onboarding docs to warn against committing real keys into test fixtures.
maya: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/payments/pull/412 (contains filter-repo log and instructions).
ben: Credentials rotated. Updated TICK-458 with rotated key IDs.
josh: Org scan: found 1 other repo with a dummy-looking fixture key (different, probably test-only). Flagged low risk and replaced with generated ephemeral key material.
sara: Great. I'll start drafting the postmortem and list follow-ups (pre-receive hook, daily scans, RBAC changes).
sec-oncall: Moving incident to status "contained". Keep ticket open for postmortem and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
